subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the range of: 14, 9, 21, 5, 17?
To find an estimate of the mean from grouped data, you divide the total of (mid-point × frequency) by:
questions.explain: Estimated mean = sum of (mid-point × frequency) ÷ total frequency.

questions.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.q: To estimate the mean of grouped data you multiply each class frequency by the class:
questions.explain: Estimated mean uses the mid-point of each class multiplied by its frequency.

questions.q: In a Venn diagram of 30 students, 12 study French only, 9 study Spanish only and 4 study both. How many study neither?
What is the mean of: 2, 4, 6, 8?
A survey only asks people leaving a gym about exercise habits. This sample is:
questions.explain: Only gym-goers are sampled, so the sample is biased toward active people.

questions.q: In a frequency table, the value 3 occurs 5 times and the value 4 occurs 2 times. What is the mode?
questions.explain: The value with the highest frequency is 3 (occurring 5 times).

questions.q: The probability a seed germinates is 0.8. Out of 250 seeds, how many are expected to germinate?
The probability a bus is late is 0.15. What is the probability it is not late?
A die is rolled 300 times and lands on 6 a total of 45 times. What is the experimental probability of a 6?
A scatter graph shows points rising from bottom-left to top-right. This is:
questions.explain: As one variable increases the other increases, showing positive correlation.

questions.q: What is the mean of: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25?
A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. What is P(red)?
Which value could NOT be a probability?
questions.explain: Probabilities lie between 0 and 1, so 1.2 is impossible.

questions.q: Probabilities for three outcomes are 0.2, 0.5 and x. What is x?
As temperature rises, sales of hot soup fall. This shows:
questions.explain: One increasing while the other decreases is negative correlation.

questions.q: What is the median of: 2, 8, 4, 6?
A fair coin is flipped twice. What is P(at least one head)?
questions.explain: P(at least one head) = 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.q: On the probability scale, what value represents a certain event?
What is the median of: 3, 1, 9, 5, 7?
A coin is flipped 200 times and lands heads 90 times. What is the experimental probability of heads?
